issues.detail: The List date 2026-11-01 is taken from the PDF metadata CreationDate. The document text and the council's page call it the 'Local Validation List September 2026', so the text-based date is September 2026. A November 2026 news item says the list was agreed, which should be checked as the possible adoption or effective date.
issues.evidence: reference_row Date basis 'PDF metadata CreationDate'; Grokbot's own captured text: 'Local Validation List September 2026 Validation Requirement'

issues.detail: Householder, Outline, Reserved matters, Advertisement consent, Lawful development cert, Prior approval, s73 and Discharge of conditions all say '(none)', yet Grokbot's own extracted text has requirements that apply to 'all development' or 'all applications'. Examples: Tree Survey/Arboricultural Assessment ('required for all development that affects any trees'), Habitat Regulations Assessment ('all development within or close to the 7km zone of influence for Ashdown Forest'), Planning Statement ('All applications'), Ecology survey, Lighting impact assessment, Heritage Statement and BNG. Outline in particular should carry the major-development items (affordable housing, transport, SCI, S106 heads of terms, LVIA).
issues.evidence: app_type_rows Householder/Outline '(none) - No specific local requirements identified'; Planning Statement trigger 'All applications Planning Statement(s)'

issues.detail: 'Contaminated Land' is placed under 'Minerals & waste (county)'. Tunbridge Wells is a district and not the minerals and waste authority. The row was triggered only because the text mentions 'landfill sites' as a past use, and the requirement belongs to ordinary planning applications. Most other rows carry the 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning' note (about 30 rows, e.g. Affordable Housing, BNG, Fire Statement, Transport). The Heritage Statement appears only under Listed building consent, not Full planning.
issues.evidence: Minerals & waste row trigger 'Ground conditions/Land Contamination Report ... such as landfill sites, former industrial and commercial processes'

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are spliced from neighbouring sections and describe a different requirement. Noise Impact Assessment's excerpt is about affordable housing tenure. The S106 Heads of Terms excerpt is about tree works ('Where trees are felled, proposals for planting replacement trees'). 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' actually quotes the retail Policy ED10 sequential test and telecoms pre-submission consultation. 'Agricultural/rural workers' dwelling' and 'Lighting' each carry the other's text. The Full planning Arboricultural row quotes the tree works (TPO) application content ('A plan (not an aerial image) showing the position of trees listed in the Description of Works').
issues.evidence: Noise row: '...provide on-site affordable housing ... Tenure type of each affordable units'; S106 row: '...Reasons for proposed work Where trees are felled...'

issues.detail: Other triggers are cut off or are bare fragments. Affordable Housing ends at 'All applications proposing or required to'. Housing mix is just 'meet Part M4(2).'. LVIA ends at 'All major or other development in the National Landscape or its' (the setting is cut off). Parking and Travel Plan repeat the same reference-list text, and Photographs is a policy reference string.
issues.evidence: Affordable Housing trigger 'Built Development) Affordable Housing Statement All applications proposing or required to'

issues.detail: Requirements visible in Grokbot's own captured text have no app-type row. These are: Supporting information for Telecommunications proposals ('Required for Telecommunication applications', pre-submission consultation information); Isolated homes in the countryside; the Viability element of 'Viability or marketing information report' (loss of employment/community uses); Ground conditions as a general requirement; and the Ashdown Forest SAMM/SANG financial contribution for development within 7km. The full PDF could not be read, so other items may also be missing.
issues.evidence: Sequential test row text: 'Supporting information for Telecommunications Proposals Required for Telecommunication applications Information required Pre-submission consultation information.'

issues.detail: Several tab items are link text, policy references or navigation rather than requirements: 'You can download a full pdf version of the checklist:', 'Tunbridge Wells Borough Council Local Validation List September 2026 PDF 699.4 KB National validation guidance can be found on the GOV.UK...', 'Links to guidance, national and local policy The Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017...', 'EN10 ... EN11 ... Also see Pre-application advice Biodiversity Net Gain Back to top', and the heading fragment 'Local Wildlife Site (LWS) ... Information required Our survey requirements are:'.

The Ashdown Forest text is captured twice, once from the web page and once from the PDF: 'Developments within the 7km zone are likely to be required to make a financial contribution...' and the EN10/EN11 policy line. Parking provision and Transport Assessment/Travel Plan share the same trigger text.

Rows mix two sources: the HTML 'national-planning-requirements-validation-guidance' page and the September 2026 PDF. Energy Statement, EIA, Open space, Structural Survey (LBC), Tree Survey (Works to trees) and Contaminated Land are sourced from the web page. Whether the web page matches the adopted PDF should be checked. The page's file-size rule (5MB per file, legacy .doc/.xls only) is also recorded as a submission rule.

summary: The September 2026 list Grokbot linked appears to be Tunbridge Wells' current list, but the List date comes from PDF metadata (Nov 2026) and the text says September 2026. The source could not be re-fetched because the WebFetch budget ran out, but Grokbot's own extracted text shows spliced or garbled triggers and most application types wrongly marked '(none)'.
